purpose: Every locked check on the platform in one line each, including those that failed. Written from the check reports and the scorecard summaries; nothing is computed here.

outcomes.disagrees: The comparison data disagree with the model
outcomes.failed: Candidate or tool rejected under its plan
outcomes.not_adopted: Partly consistent; not adopted under the plan's rule
outcomes.inconclusive: Cannot be decided from the data available

findings.question: Does Hughes 2019 predict how exposure rises with kidney impairment (CC-5013-PK-001)?
findings.headline: Mild consistent; moderate and severe exposure under-predicted.

findings.question: Does Kim 2026 predict how exposure rises with kidney impairment (CC-5013-PK-001)?
findings.headline: Mild and moderate consistent; severe under-predicted in the primary scenario.

findings.question: Do the first two results hold with virtual subjects matched to the study?
findings.headline: Hughes unchanged; Kim's consistent moderate result disappears. Both under-predict moderate and severe.

findings.question: Do Hughes and Kim hold in myeloma patients (Bridoux 2016)?
findings.headline: Both under-predict moderate and severe again, so the non-cancer population of CC-5013-PK-001 does not explain the gap.

findings.question: Does the elimination-pathway model, calibrated on normal kidney function, predict the impaired groups of the same study?
findings.headline: Secretion-preserved reading rejected; intact-nephron reading consistent in mild and severe, under-predicts moderate (0.79 of observed AUC).

findings.question: Does it extend to end-stage kidney disease on non-dialysis days?
findings.headline: Over-predicts 1.31-fold with no residual function, consistent at 5-10 mL/min; residual function of the subjects not reported.

findings.question: Does a model in which secretion falls faster than filtration fit better?
findings.headline: Three of four deciding comparisons consistent, so not adopted. The current model is consistent with both myeloma studies in moderate and severe impairment.

findings.question: Does the body map's one-compartment time course reproduce peaks and half-lives?
findings.headline: Peak under-predicted in every group, including normal (367 vs 568 ng/mL); half-life consistent in moderate and severe.

findings.question: Does a two-compartment version, nothing fitted, do better?
findings.headline: Peak consistent in 2 of 4 groups (3 needed) and the moderate half-life got worse, so the body map keeps version 1.

findings.question: Does the constant-clearance bortezomib model match Ogawa 2008 on days 1 and 11?
findings.headline: Day 1 exposure 2.9-fold too high; the rise from day 1 to day 11 is 1.9-fold against 5.1-fold observed.

findings.question: Does the Kuan 2012 model fix the day 1 to day 11 rise?
findings.headline: No: under neither reading of its saturable term does it reproduce the rise; candidate rejected.

findings.question: Does the model match a second study (CAN-1004, 72 h sampling)?
findings.headline: Day 1 consistent; day 11 under-predicted (127 vs 241 ng.h/mL). Both studies show a larger rise than a constant clearance allows.

findings.question: Can an empirical clearance that falls over repeated doses explain the rise?
findings.headline: Neither one-parameter form reached the CAN-1004 day 11 exposure, so neither was tested on Ogawa; candidates rejected.

findings.question: Does the Iwasaki 2020 target-binding PBPK model explain the rise?
findings.headline: No: day 1 over-predicted (107 vs 46.5 ng.h/mL), day 11/day 1 ratio 2.0 vs 5.1; it behaves like constant clearance. Candidate rejected.

findings.question: Does the model match a third study (MMY-3021, day 11)?
findings.headline: Day 11 exposure consistent only at the edge and not robust; peak under-predicted (111 vs 223 ng/mL).

findings.question: Does the model reproduce Reece 2011, the study its source compared it with?
findings.headline: Not reproduced: day 1 exposure about 2-fold too high at both doses; rise to day 11 1.5-fold against 2.4-3.1.

findings.question: Does the platelet model reproduce its own fitting data?
findings.headline: Consistent with the cycle 1 day 11 fall only with concentrations in ng/mL and the effect term as printed.

findings.question: Does Gupta 2017 match the dedicated renal and hepatic impairment studies?
findings.headline: Myeloma with normal kidney function consistent; solid-tumour and hepatic groups under-predicted about 1.4-fold; peaks 2-4-fold low, so only AUC is shown.

findings.question: Does Luo 2021 match GEN501 and SIRIUS first-dose data?
findings.headline: Peaks and 8 mg/kg AUC consistent; first-week AUC at 16 mg/kg over-predicted (observed 0.87 of model).

findings.question: Does the result hold with each study's own demographics?
findings.headline: The 16 mg/kg over-prediction widens (0.83); the albumin effect predicts the two studies in the opposite order.

findings.question: Can a curve built from the POMALYST label reproduce the label's own exposure?
findings.headline: The myeloma-only parameter set passes (Cmax 71.6 vs 75 ng/mL); the label's pooled clearance and volume ranges would predict about half and fail.

findings.question: Is the label curve consistent with the Li 2017 population model?
findings.headline: Consistent (AUC 860 vs Li 780; dialysis fold 1.38 in both). Model to model, not observed data.

findings.question: Can a one-compartment curve from the EVOMELA label reproduce its exposure?
findings.headline: Not eligible: peak under-predicted (3.64 vs 5.8 ug/mL), and the label's clearance and volume imply a 197-minute half-life against the stated 75.

findings.question: Can a curve from the HEMADY label reproduce its exposure?
findings.headline: Passes: clearance and AUC within 1%; peak 186 vs 247 ng/mL (ratio 0.75), within the plan's limits.

findings.question: Is the dexamethasone curve consistent with the NEOFORDEX studies?
findings.headline: Consistent on the primary endpoint and both AUCs; patients' apparent clearance was lower than the label's, a caveat shown with the curve.

findings.question: Does the rule-based eligibility extractor meet its accuracy thresholds?
findings.headline: All eight criterion types failed (precision 0.73-0.83, recall 0.64-0.80); version 2 was planned with a new 200-trial sample.
